sections.text:
In a small village located on the outskirts of a dense, dark forest, there lived a beautiful girl who was very loved by everyone.

The girl always wore a hat and a red coat, given to her by her old grandmother, whom she loved very much.

Because of this dress, everyone in the village began to call her “Laila in Red.”

Laila was a kind and innocent girl who loved playing in nature and helping her mother with the housework.

One sunny day, the mother called Laila and said to her: “Laila, your old grandmother has fallen ill and she is lying in her bed feeling weak.”

She gave her a little basket containing fresh cakes, some delicious pies, and a bottle of juice to strengthen her.

The mother warned her daughter, saying: “Go to your grandmother’s hut, which is located on the other side of the forest, but listen carefully. Beware of straying from the main road, and beware of talking to strangers, no matter what.”

Laila promised her mother to be careful, took the basket and headed towards the forest, singing happily.

The forest was peaceful and beautiful, full of colorful wildflowers and butterflies flying from flower to flower.

Laila forgot her mother's warning over time, and began to move a little away from the road to pick some beautiful flowers to make her grandmother happy.

Meanwhile, a large, cunning wolf was watching her from behind the trees, feeling very hungry.

The wolf approached her maliciously, pretended to be gentle, and said in a soft voice: “Good morning, Little Red Riding Hood. Where are you going on this beautiful morning?”

The innocent Laila did not realize the danger of the wolf, and she answered him innocently: “I am going to my grandmother’s hut to give her these cakes because she is sick.”

The cunning wolf asked: “And where is your grandmother’s hut, my little one?”

“It's at the end of the forest, under the three big oak trees,” Laila answered.

The wolf drew an evil plan in his head, and said to Laila: “Look at those wonderful flowers over there. Why don’t you pick more of them for your grandmother? That will make her very happy.”

Laila was convinced by the wolf's idea and began collecting more flowers, which delayed her arrival.

The wolf seized the opportunity and ran as fast as he could, heading directly to the grandmother's hut, far ahead of Laila.

When the wolf arrived, he gently knocked on the door, and the grandmother from inside asked in a weak voice: “Who is at the door?”

The wolf imitated Laila's voice and said: "I am your granddaughter, Laila, grandmother. I brought you food."

The grandmother said: “Open the door, my daughter, it is not locked.”

The wolf quickly entered, attacked the poor grandmother and swallowed her in one bite!
Then he took Grandma's nightgown, hat, and glasses, dressed them, and covered herself with the quilt in bed to wait for Laila.

After a while, Laila arrived at the hut and knocked on the door. The wolf said in a rough voice that he tried to soften: “Come in, my daughter.”

Laila entered and noticed that the hut was dark, and that her grandmother looked very strange in bed.

Laila approached and said in surprise: “Grandma, why are your ears so big?”

The wolf replied: “To hear them better, my child.”

Laila said: “Grandma, why are your eyes so big?”

The wolf replied: “To see you better in them, my child.”

Laila said as she felt her fear increasing: “But, grandmother.

Why are your teeth so big and sharp?!”

Here the wolf revealed his true face and shouted: “I will eat you with it faster!!”.

The wolf jumped out of bed, attacked Laila, and swallowed her too in one fell swoop!
After this hearty meal, the wolf felt very sleepy, so he lay down on the bed and began to snore very loudly.

The snoring was so loud that a brave woodsman who was passing by the hut heard it. He was surprised by the sound and expected that the grandmother was in danger.

The woodcutter entered the hut carrying his axe, and saw the wolf sleeping with an abnormally swollen stomach.

The smart woodcutter realized what had happened, so he took large scissors and cut the dead wolf's stomach very carefully.

What a joy! Little Laila came out alive and gasping in fear, followed by her grandmother’s exit as well, and she was fine but exhausted.

Laila and the grandmother thanked the brave woodcutter for saving them, and they all sat eating the cakes that Laila had brought.

Laila in the red dress learned a lesson that she will never forget for the rest of her life: to always listen to the advice of her parents, not to stray from the path, and not to talk to strangers, no matter how nice they seem.

Since that day, Laila and her grandmother lived safely, and no wolf approached their village after that incident.
